Threat Scenario: Employee opens malicious attachment/link that drops a loader and ransomware
Existing Controls: Annual awareness training; basic spam filter
Recommended Treatment: Monthly phishing simulations; email sandboxing; report-phish button

Threat Scenario: Attacker uses stolen credentials on VPN/RDP exposed to the internet
Recommended Treatment: Phishing-resistant MFA; close public RDP; geo/IP restrictions

Threat Scenario: Exploitation of known CVEs on edge devices and web servers
Recommended Treatment: 72-hour SLA for actively exploited CVEs (CISA KEV); attack-surface scanning

Threat Scenario: Attacker escalates to domain admin and deploys ransomware domain-wide
Recommended Treatment: Privileged Access Management; tiered admin model; LAPS; remove standing admin rights

Threat Scenario: Ransomware spreads rapidly across servers and workstations
Recommended Treatment: Segment crown jewels; restrict SMB/RDP east-west; micro-segmentation

Threat Scenario: Attacker deletes or encrypts backups before detonation
Recommended Treatment: 3-2-1-1-0 strategy; immutable/air-gapped copy; separate backup credentials with MFA

Threat Scenario: Data stolen before encryption and leaked to force payment
Recommended Treatment: Data classification; DLP; egress filtering; encryption at rest

Threat Scenario: Backups fail or are slow to restore when needed
Recommended Treatment: Quarterly restore tests; verify integrity and malware-free before restore

Risk: No EDR on endpoints and servers
Threat Scenario: Ransomware executes undetected on unmanaged or legacy-AV hosts
Recommended Treatment: Deploy EDR with ransomware behaviour rules and auto-isolation

Threat Scenario: Intrusion goes unnoticed for days before encryption
Recommended Treatment: Central SIEM; MDR/SOC 24/7; alerts for mass file changes and backup tampering

Threat Scenario: Recovery not prioritised by business criticality
Recommended Treatment: Complete BIA; define RTO/RPO; rank systems for restoration

Threat Scenario: Stolen browser-saved credentials sold and used for access
Recommended Treatment: Password manager; MFA everywhere; dark-web credential monitoring

Threat Scenario: Slow, uncoordinated response increases dwell time and damage
Recommended Treatment: Ransomware playbook; biannual tabletop exercises; IR retainer

Threat Scenario: Vendor or MSP compromised and used to push ransomware
Recommended Treatment: Vendor risk assessments; security clauses; least-privilege vendor access

Threat Scenario: Recovery of critical systems takes weeks
Recommended Treatment: Update DR plan; restoration runbooks; clean-room recovery environment

Threat Scenario: Unpatchable systems are easy targets and halt operations when encrypted
Recommended Treatment: Isolate legacy systems; virtual patching; compensating controls

Threat Scenario: Unknown systems stay unpatched and unmonitored, becoming entry points
Recommended Treatment: Automated discovery; CMDB; owner assigned to each asset

Threat Scenario: Scans run irregularly; findings not prioritised by exploitability
Recommended Treatment: Continuous scanning; risk-based prioritisation; remediation tracking KPIs

Risk: Poor crisis communication and legal notification
Threat Scenario: Delayed regulator/customer/staff notification causes fines and reputational loss
Recommended Treatment: Comms plan; legal counsel on call; regulatory notification matrix

Threat Scenario: Weak oversight leads to underfunded controls and unclear risk appetite
Recommended Treatment: Quarterly board reporting; documented cyber risk appetite; KPIs/KRIs

Threat Scenario: Same weaknesses repeat across incidents
Recommended Treatment: Mandatory lessons-learned reviews; track corrective actions

Threat Scenario: Ad hoc payment decision without legal, sanctions or insurance review
Recommended Treatment: Documented decision framework; sanctions screening; cyber insurance review
